metadata.description: Validated single-file dataset selected from compile/run-passing candidates only.

samples.docstring: // Returns a random base64 encoded string from crypto/rand.
// RandomKey returns a random 16-byte base64 alphabet string
// UUID generates a ploop UUID
// GenerateUUID is used to generate a random UUID

// The uuid function is used by the sentry collector to generate unique event
// IDs.
// randUint32 returns a random 32bit uint from the CSPRNG

// letterOnlyMapF is used in conjunction with strings.Map to return
// only the characters A-Z and a-z in a string
// NewSeed returns a cryptographically secure seed
// Gets the buildpack directory

// transportFromEnv builds a http transport from environment variables, adding
// a HTTP proxy if HTTP_PROXY or HTTPS_PROXY has been set.

// EnsureUserAddressDir sets sticky bit on XDG_RUNTIME_DIR if XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is set.
// See https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/issues/1694

// BinPath returns path to the keybase executable. If the executable path is a
// symlink, the target path is returned.
// Getwd returns a absolute path of the current directory.

// DefaultSourceTree returns the /src directory of the first entry in $GOPATH.
// If $GOPATH is empty, it returns "./". Useful as a default output location.
// Geted returns an absolute path to the executable.
// EnableIPv6Forwarding sets proc file to enable IPv6 forwarding

// GoPath returns either $GOPATH or the new $HOME/go path
// introduced with Go 1.8
// GetCurrentDir gets the directory where the application was run
// BestEffortSystemCertPool returns system cert pool as best effort, otherwise an empty cert pool
// tempfile returns a temporary file for use
// GetOpenFileDescriptorCount returns the number of open file descriptors for the process id of the caller.
// Setup the mocking files for the stdout and the stderr.

// Generates a time ordered UUID. Top 32 bits are a timestamp,
// bottom 96 are random.

// ListenAddress returns the host:[port] network address, derived from the environment,
// that the application should listen on.
// mustGetSystemCertPool - return system CAs or empty pool in case of error (or windows)
// otherSource serves as a placeholder from some other source of user input.
// GetMaxThreads returns the maximum number of threads that the system can create.
// IsWorker returns whether the current process is an einhorn worker.
// Umask extracts the umask from env
// Hostname reads HOSTNAME env var or os.Hostname used for your app
// GetExecPath returns the path to the current binary
// Path returns program's full filename
// CountListeners returns the number of listener fd's passed by the master.
// GPGOpts parses extra GPG options from the environment

// getDefaultMoniker returns a default moniker, which is the host name. If runtime
// fails to get the host name, "anonymous" will be returned.
// Returns the desired child environment, properly filtered and added to.
// AppArmorProfile returns the current apparmor profile.

// See: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7922270/obtain-users-home-directory
// we can't cross compile using cgo and use user.Current()

// GetUsernameFromEnv returns the user name from the environment variable
// for the actual process.

// unixLocale returns the locale by checking the $LC_ALL, $LC_CTYPE, and $LANG
// environment variables. If none of those are set, it returns "US-ASCII".
// GetCredentials returns back the username and the password.
// GOPATH return GOPATH from env
// this simulates the results of http.Request's ParseForm() function
// lineFromConsole reads a line from stdin
// successive Fibonacci numbers.

// DefaultVerifyOptions returns VerifyOptions that use the system root certificates, current time,
// and requires certificates to be valid for client auth (x509.ExtKeyUsageClientAuth)

// FindCWD returns the current working directory from where the Hugo
// executable is run.
// scriptDir returns the absolute path of the running process.
// Generate a random string of 8 chars, needed for OAuth signature
// successive Fibonacci numbers.

// NewTraceID is a trace ID creation algorithm which produces values that are
// compatible with AWS X-Ray.

// reorder to default to the highest level of security.  See:
// https://blog.bracebin.com/achieving-perfect-ssl-labs-score-with-go
// Command line used to run tool
// Fibonacci returns successive Fibonacci numbers starting from 1
// successive Fibonacci numbers.

// fibonacci is a function that returns
// a function that returns an int.

// NewID is a span ID creation algorithm which produces values that are
// compatible with AWS X-Ray.
